author: marketing_c
protectedRevelations: Longview architecture, funding instruments and duty-of-inquiry prescriptions

scenes.title: Permission before proof
scenes.viewerPurpose: Make the distinctive idea or tension understandable on first hearing. Introduce the book-specific proposal clearly and leave its fuller explanation for reading.
scenes.composition: An untested prototype waits between its inventor and reviewer
addOrChange: Add a bounded test proposal and avoid a simple yes-or-no verdict.

cues.narration: Your idea needs proof to win support, but producing proof needs support first.
cues.visualAction: The reviewer needs evidence that the inventor needs resources to produce.

cues.narration: The Permission Paradox proposes a way to test ideas caught inside that circle.
cues.visualAction: Place the proposed small test beside the unresolved evidence gap.

scenes.title: Two reasonable viewpoints
scenes.viewerPurpose: Understand why both inventors and reviewers hesitate See a promising idea lost between them
scenes.composition: Both people have legitimate questions about one prototype
addOrChange: Remove the imagined pipe failure and add benefit and evidence notes.

cues.narration: Inventors imagine something new; reviewers want evidence that it will work.
cues.visualAction: The inventor names the possible benefit while the reviewer asks for proof.

cues.narration: Both have reasons, and a promising idea can disappear between them.
cues.visualAction: Hold the same prototype between the two unanswered concerns.

scenes.title: The smallest useful test
scenes.viewerPurpose: Notice AI making more proposals without more tests Wonder how an unfamiliar idea could get a fair test
scenes.composition: Two proposals wait for one test bench
addOrChange: Remove the extended leak outcome and clearly mark a small test boundary.

cues.narration: AI makes the mismatch sharper by producing proposals faster than institutions can test them.
cues.visualAction: Another proposal arrives while the first test is still being prepared.

cues.narration: The book asks how we might test an unfamiliar idea before accepting or dismissing it.
cues.visualAction: Choose a limited test setup and leave the result blank.

scenes.title: Give possibility a hearing
scenes.viewerPurpose: Connect the dilemma to your own uncertain projects Ask how fairness can coexist with careful judgment
scenes.composition: A shared record states what the next test would need to show
addOrChange: Remove deployment approval and keep alternative outcomes open.

cues.narration: Its cases speak to researchers, founders, and anyone responsible for judging uncertain work.
cues.visualAction: Both people read the same proposed evidence record.

cues.narration: What would give unfamiliar ideas a fair hearing without making every persuasive claim credible?
cues.visualAction: End on the testable question rather than an approved invention.
